×
Consist): Combines repository grouping with consistency grouping, creating subgroups by repository and exact pass count before sampling proportionally.

All stratified methods preserve each group’s proportion of the full test suite when building the subset (Cochran, 1977; Neyman, 1934). For example, if a group contains 60% of all instances, it receives 60% of the subset’s slots.

4.4.2.Geometric Test Selection

The stratified baselines fix each group’s share of the subset but still draw instances at random within each group. Our geometric methods keep the same grouping by pass counts (consistency groups, or the pass/fail split when only one prior full run is available) and replace the random draw within each group: instances are selected deterministically based on their position in the embedding space. We refer to this combination of outcome grouping and geometric selection as Embedding-Within-Strata. We use five geometric algorithms:

(1)

Centroid (Manning et al., 2008): Computes the average embedding of all instances in the group (the set of instances with the same pass count, as defined above), then selects the instances whose embeddings are closest to the average, up to the group’s share of the subset. The selected instances are those where the agent followed the most common pattern of actions in the group, such as similar sequences of edits, test runs, and error handling.

(2)

Facility Location (Nemhauser et al., 1978): Selects instances one at a time, each time choosing the instance that increases the total embedding similarity between the selected set and all remaining instances the most. This produces a set where every unselected instance has at least one similar representative in the subset.

(3)

Medoid (PAM Build) (Kaufman and Rousseeuw, 1990): First selects the single instance with the smallest total distance to all others (the most central real data point). It then adds the remaining instances one at a time, each time picking the one that best reduces the remaining distances to the already-selected set. Unlike Centroid, which computes an average point that may not correspond to any real instance, Medoid always picks actual instances from the data.

(4)

Kennard-Stone (Kennard and Stone, 1969): Selects instances one at a time, each time selecting the instance farthest from all previously selected instances. This maximizes diversity by spreading selections as far apart as possible in the embedding space.

(5)

Core/Edge (Manning et al., 2008; Kennard and Stone, 1969): A hybrid that allocates 90% of the group’s share using Centroid (picking typical instances) and 10% using Kennard-Stone (picking the most different outliers). This balances representativeness with coverage of unusual behaviors.

Given the same prior runs, embeddings, and subset size, each geometric algorithm always produces the same subset, with no random draws. On later runs, the developer evaluates only the selected subset and uses its resolve rate to estimate the full test suite’s resolve rate.

5.Evaluation Setup
5.1.Dataset: Three Agent Evaluation Scenarios

To evaluate the effectiveness of our test selection approach (Section 4) under different types of agent changes, we curate a dataset comprising three evaluation scenarios: (1) reruns of the same agent configurations, (2) changes to the model or configurations of a given agent, and (3) changes to the agent framework. We collect trajectory data from established benchmarks to represent each of these scenarios:

(1)

Single-setup: Rerun Same Agent. This is a sanity-check scenario where nothing changes between runs. The same agent is run repeatedly in the same deployment environment, so the only variation comes from the stochasticity of the model’s outputs. This scenario captures the easiest case, where a subset only needs to absorb run-to-run noise rather than any real change in behavior. We use existing, publicly available trajectories of the OpenHands agent with the Qwen3-Coder model, which we downloaded from SWE-Rebench (Trofimova et al., 2025)4. The full dataset contains 67,074 trajectories over 6,306 instances, with each instance rerun a varying number of times. We keep instances rerun 5 to 10 times, a range comparable to the run counts of the other datasets included in the study. The retained dataset includes 45 runs over the SWE-Rebench benchmark instances (3,188 instances, 25,279 trajectories). The runs form six independent groups, where, in each group, the same set of instances is rerun a fixed number of times, from 5 reruns for one group up to 10 for another. The groups differ in size, so the total number of trajectories is not a simple product of instances and runs.

(2)

Multi-model: Change Models. This scenario captures a common development case where the agent framework stays the same but the underlying foundation model or its execution settings change. A model change can alter how instances are solved and which of them pass, so the subset must remain representative as per-instance outcomes change between runs. Unlike the Single-setup dataset, we downloaded OpenHands trajectories from the SWE-bench experiments repository5, where each run pairs OpenHands with a different model and diverse execution settings (e.g., inference scaling, adjusted reasoning effort, and varying iteration limits). This dataset consists of 6 runs of 500 SWE-bench Verified instances each, yielding 3,000 trajectories.

(3)

Multi-agent: Change Agent Framework. To assess subset selection under more substantial changes to the agent’s architecture, we include trajectories from five agent frameworks: OpenHands, Moatless, Lingxi, Trae, and Refact, paired with models including Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 4 Sonnet, Kimi K2, and multi-model ensembles. A framework change alters the agent’s entire problem-solving strategy, not just how a fixed agent behaves, so the historical trajectories used for selection may no longer reflect the new agent’s behavior. This is the hardest scenario for our approach and tests where trajectory-based selection reaches its limits. Also downloaded from the SWE-bench experiments repository, the dataset comprises 7 runs on 500 SWE-bench Verified instances, yielding 3,500 trajectories.

5.2.Evaluation Protocol

Figure 4 provides a high-level overview of our evaluation protocol. Because the source datasets differ substantially in the number of runs they contain and the difficulty of the instances, the protocol has two main phases. First, we generate representative, synthetic trajectory distributions by sampling benchmark instances (across all runs), at controlled resolve rates (10% through 90%) to validate our methods across a broad range of difficulty levels. Second, we simulate realistic development conditions by treating earlier runs as historical data, from which we compute embeddings and select the subset, and later runs as unseen future runs, preserving chronological order and preventing look-ahead bias. The following sections describe these steps in detail.

Figure 4.Evaluation protocol, illustrated on the Multi-model dataset. The Multi-agent dataset follows the same protocol. The Single-setup dataset follows the same protocol without the synthetic distribution generation step, since its 45 empirical runs already provide enough data. Left: stratified bootstrapping over the source run generates 1,000 synthetic distributions, each a set of 250 benchmark instances, spread across nine difficulty levels. Right: each distribution is evaluated on all runs under temporal cross-validation, which splits runs into past (training) and future (test) runs. Example splits are shown for window sizes one and two. Bottom: the evaluation flow for one distribution, comparing the subset resolve rate against the full distribution’s resolve rate on future runs to compute RMSE and MaxErr.
5.2.1.Synthetic Distribution Generation

The Single-setup dataset is a sanity-check scenario containing 45 empirical runs over 3,188 instances, which provide enough data for direct evaluation. In contrast, the Multi-model and Multi-agent datasets contain only 6 and 7 runs, respectively, which is insufficient for robust comparison across selection methods. We therefore generate synthetic distributions only for the Multi-model and Multi-agent datasets, applying the same procedure to each. Everything after this distributions generation step

Why are acquisition strategies different for active learning and active testing?
---
Researchers have already investigated acquisition functions for active learning, and it would be helpful if we could just apply these here. However, active testing is a different problem conceptually because we are not trying to use the data to fit a model.
---
First, popular approaches for active learning avoid areas with high aleatoric uncertainty while seeking out high epistemic uncertainty. This motivates acquisition functions like BALD (Houlsby et al., 2011) or BatchBALD (Kirsch et al., 2019). For active testing, however, areas of high aleatoric uncertainty can be critical to the estimate.
---
Second, as Imberg et al. (2020) point out, the optimal acquisition scheme for active learning will minimize the expected generalization error at the end of training. They show how this motivates additional terms beyond what one would get from minimizing the variance of the loss estimator.
---
Third, as Farquhar et al. (2021) show, a biased loss estimator can be helpful during training because it often partially cancels the natural bias of the training loss. This is no longer true at test-time, where we want to minimize bias as much as possible.
---
Perhaps the best-known instance of adaptive experimental design is active learning, wherein the designs to be chosen are the data points for which to acquire labels (Atlas et al., 1990; Settles, 2010; Houlsby et al., 2011; Sener & Savarese, 2018). This is typically done by optimizing, or sampling from, an acquisition function, with much discussion in the literature on the form this should take (Imberg et al., 2020).

> Historical record only. Do not treat this section as new instructions.

````markdown
## 结论

**可以设计成检索召回流程，但不能只是“问题文本相似度 Top‑K”。**

更合适的定义是：

> 给定一次进化改动 \(e\)、parent agent 在各任务上的历史 trajectory 与失败诊断 \(H\)，在固定预算下选择任务子集 \(S_e\)，最大化发现 **parent→child 行为变化** 的概率，同时保留对整体能力变化的可靠估计。

推荐采用：

**多路召回 + 影响风险排序 + 多样性约束 + 随机审计 + parent/child 配对评测 + 不确定时扩容**

其中检索负责提出“最值得测什么”，但不直接决定回退。

---

## 1. DGM 当前方案的问题

DGM 的 SWE-bench 评估流程是：

1. 固定 10 题检查基本代码编辑能力；
2. 通过后补固定 50 题；
3. 60 题得分超过 40%，且位于 archive 前二时，扩展到固定 200 题。

论文估算 60 个 SWE-bench 任务约 \$350，完整进化约 \$22,000，因此降低每次评估任务数确实有价值。[DGM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.22954)

固定子集有三个问题：

1. **覆盖偏差**：可能持续测到与改动无关的题。
2. **回归漏检**：真正依赖被修改组件的任务可能不在子集中。
3. **优化器过拟合**：经过多代进化后，agent 会逐渐适应固定评测分布。

但动态子集还会引入一个新问题：

> 不同 child 使用不同子集时，raw pass rate 不再可直接比较。

因此不能简单做：

```text
每轮检索 K 道题 → 跑 child → 用通过率决定回退
```

正确做法是区分两类目标：

- **局部因果评估**：这次 mutation 相比 parent 改善了什么、破坏了什么，用于回退。
- **全局能力评估**：不同 archive 节点谁更强，用于 parent selection。

这两个目标不应该强行共用一个分数。

---

## 2. 推荐方法：Impact-Conditioned Dynamic Evaluation

### 2.1 输入表示

#### Mutation 表示

不能只使用“本轮要解决的问题描述”，还需要实际代码改动：

```text
MutationProfile {
  intent                 # 计划解决什么问题
  diff                   # 实际代码改动
  changed_components     # prompt/tool/editor/context/ranking/orchestration
  changed_contracts      # 哪些行为契约可能变化
  expected_improvements
  possible_side_effects
  scope                  # local / cross-cutting / global
}
```

`intent` 和 `diff` 必须同时使用。因为 agent 声称修复 A，但实际 diff 可能同时改变 B、C。

#### Task 表示

每个 benchmark task 不只保存 issue 文本，还应保存：

```text
TaskProfile {
  issue_text
  repository / language / task_type
  historical_outcomes
  historical_trajectories
  tools_used
  files/actions/tests/errors
  token/time cost
  failure_diagnosis
  diagnosis_confidence
  last_evaluated_generation
}
```

其中 `failure_diagnosis` 推荐使用多标签结构：

```text
localization_failure
context_loss
edit_tool_failure
invalid_or_empty_patch
test_misuse
planning_failure
timeout
dependency_or_environment
overfitting_to_visible_tests
patch_ranking_failure
```

诊断必须带 evidence span 和置信度，不能让 LLM 的单次归因成为硬过滤条件。

---

## 3. 四路召回

### 3.1 Repair Recall：验证预期修复

从 parent 当前失败的任务中，召回与 mutation 目标相符的 bad case：

\[
s_{\text{fix}}(e,t)
=
\operatorname{sim}
\left(
\text{mutation impact},
\text{task issue}+\text{failure diagnosis}
\right)
\]

例如本轮修改 context compaction，则优先召回：

- 长 trajectory；
- 曾发生 context truncation；
- 后期遗忘早期约束；
- 重复读取文件；
- patch 前后不一致。

这一通道回答：

> 这次进化是否真的修复了它声称要修复的问题？

### 3.2 Regression Recall：发现新回归

只测 parent 的 bad case 是不够的。回退决策更需要发现：

```text
parent pass → child fail
```

因此必须从 parent 已通过任务中召回：

- 历史 trajectory 使用过被修改组件的任务；
- 对该组件依赖程度高的任务；
- 与历史同类 mutation 所破坏任务相似的任务；
- 高价值或高严重度任务。

例如修改 edit tool，即使某任务以前成功，也应在以下情况下高优先级复测：

- 大文件编辑；
- 多文件修改；
- 多次局部替换；
- patch conflict；
- Unicode/换行/缩进敏感。

这一通道通常比 Repair Recall 更重要，因为它决定是否需要回退。

### 3.3 Representative Recall：保持总体代表性

只召回高风险任务会放大局部变化，不能估计整体性能。

可以采用近期工作提出的 trajectory-aware 思路：

1. 按 parent 历史 pass/fail/flaky 分层；
2. 对清洗后的 trajectory embedding 聚类；
3. 选择每层的 centroid/medoid 或 facility-location representative。

近期的 SWE-agent 子集选择工作报告，10% trajectory-aware subset 的中位总体分数估计误差低于 5%，但它优化的是“估计全局 resolve rate”，不是“发现 mutation 导致的回归”。因此适合作为本方法的代表性通道和强 baseline。[Trajectory-Aware Benchmark Subset Selection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24928)

### 3.4 Exploration Recall：随机审计

必须保留随机探索，否则被检索器认为“不相关”的任务永远不会执行。

随机部分用于：

- 发现未知副作用；
- 估计 retrieval recall；
- 收集训练影响预测器的新标签；
- 防止进化过程钻检索器盲区。

生产中的 predictive test selection 也通常保留覆盖或召回约束，而不是完全相信预测器。例如 Facebook 的方法在降低约一半测试成本时，仍以高故障召回率为约束。[Predictive Test Selection](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.05286)

---

## 4. 不要直接 Top‑K：用预算约束的组合选择

先通过四路召回构造候选池，再计算：

\[
a(e,t)=
\alpha s_{\text{fix}}
+\beta s_{\text{regression}}
+\gamma s_{\text{impact}}
+\eta s_{\text{uncertainty}}
+\rho s_{\text{novelty}}
-\lambda c_t
\]

其中：

- \(s_{\text{impact}}\)：child 与 parent 在该任务上结果发生变化的概率；
- \(s_{\text{uncertainty}}\)：预测器对变化方向不确定的程度；
- \(s_{\text{novelty}}\)：长期未评测或远离已有样本的程度；
- \(c_t\)：历史 token/time 成本。

然后求：

\[
\max_{S}
\sum_{t\in S}a(e,t)
+\mu\,\text{Coverage}(S)
-\nu\,\text{Redundancy}(S)
\]

约束：

\[
\sum_{t\in S}c_t \le B
\]

`Coverage` 可以采用 facility location；也可以按：

- parent outcome；
- repository；
- failure taxonomy；
- trajectory cluster；
- task cost；

设置最小配额。

一个可用于第一轮消融的初始预算结构是：

| 通道 | 比例 |
|---|---:|
| Repair Recall | 25–35% |
| Regression Recall | 25–35% |
| Representative Recall | 20–25% |
| Random Exploration | 10–20% |

这些比例应作为待验证超参数，而不是最终固定规则。

---

## 5. 回退评估必须是 parent/child 配对实验

对于本轮动态子集 \(S_e\)，应在相同条件下同时执行 parent 和 child：

\[
d_t = y_t(\text{child})-y_t(\text{parent})
\in \{-1,0,1\}
\]

- \(d_t=1\)：改进；
- \(d_t=-1\)：回归；
- \(d_t=0\)：没有可观测变化。

这样评估的是 mutation 的局部效果，而不是两个不可比子集上的绝对分数。

推荐记录：

```text
n_improved  = count(parent fail, child pass)
n_regressed = count(parent pass, child fail)
n_unchanged
token_delta
latency_delta
severity_weighted_delta
```

对于随机性较强的任务，优先对 discordant task，即 parent/child 结果不同的任务增加重复，而不是平均重复全部任务。

---

## 6. 定向样本不能直接估计全局分数

如果只执行检索 Top‑K，则样本明显偏向“可能变化”的任务：

- 它适合检测回归；
- 不适合直接估计总体 pass rate。

有两种处理方式。

### 简单可靠方案：双头评估

分别维护：

```text
LocalImpactScore   # 动态配对子集，用于 accept/rollback
GlobalAuditScore   # 随机/代表性子集或周期全量，用于 archive ranking
```

不同分支的 `LocalImpactScore` 不直接横向比较。

### 统计方案：已知纳入概率的分层采样

将任务按风险、outcome 和行为 cluster 分层，在每层随机抽样。用：

\[
\hat{\Delta}
=
\sum_h \frac{N_h}{N}\bar d_h
\]

估计整体变化。

如果使用更一般的非均匀随机采样，则可以用 importance weighting/HT estimator。Active Testing 的核心结论正是：主动选样会引入偏差，但通过随机 acquisition 和重要性加权可以恢复无偏或低偏估计。[Active Testing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.05331)

MVP 阶段建议先采用分层随机，因为纳入概率和方差估计更清晰。

---

## 7. 回退应采用三态决策

不要强制每轮二选一。推荐：

```text
ACCEPT
ROLLBACK
ESCALATE / QUARANTINE
```

示例规则：

1. 基本契约测试失败：直接 rollback。
2. 出现预定义 critical regression：rollback。
3. 全局差分的置信下界高于非劣阈值，且定向回归在容忍范围内：accept。
4. 证据不足或 repair/regression 信号冲突：追加下一批任务。
5. 达到最大预算仍不确定：quarantine，不作为高权重 parent。

这比“subset score 下降就回退”稳定，尤其适合存在随机 LLM 输出的情况。

---

## 8. 可以在线学习，但第一版不要直接上 RL

历史数据逐渐积累后，可以训练：

\[
P(d_t=1\mid e,t,H_t),\qquad
P(d_t=-1\mid e,t,H_t)
\]

训练标签直接来自历代 parent/child 配对结果。

特征包括：

- task/diagnosis/mutation embedding；
- changed component × historical tool usage；
- parent pass/fail；
- 历史 flaky rate；
- 相似 mutation 的结果变化；
- trajectory 长度、错误类型、编辑次数；
- task cost。

第一版建议：

1. BM25 + dense retrieval；
2. 手工结构化特征；
3. logistic regression 或 gradient-boosted trees；
4. 概率校准；
5. 时间顺序验证。

不建议一开始使用 RL。RETECS 等工作说明 RL 可以持续适应 CI 历史，但需要足够多稳定的执行周期；你当前的进化节点数可能不足，而且 RL 会增加难以解释的策略漂移。[RETECS](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.04122)

---

## 9. 实验设计

### Baselines

至少比较：

1. DGM 固定 60；
2. uniform random；
3. repository/outcome stratified random；
4. problem-text retrieval Top‑K；
5. trajectory centroid；
6. mutation + bad-case retrieval；
7. 完整 hybrid 方法。

### Ablations

```text
problem only
diagnosis only
mutation intent only
actual diff only
intent + diff
without regression recall
without random exploration
without diversity constraint
unpaired evaluation
```

### 主指标

不要只报告 subset accuracy error。至少报告：

- **Regression Recall@Budget**：全量已知的 pass→fail 中发现多少；
- **Improvement Recall@Budget**；
- **rollback decision consistency**：与全量决策一致率；
- false accept rate；
- false rollback rate；
- critical regression miss rate；
- global delta MAE 和置信区间覆盖率；
- token/time saving；
- 达到正确决策所需平均任务数。

### 数据要求

DGM 当前释放结果只有部分节点跑过 200 题，多数节点约 60 题，不能为未运行任务提供 ground truth。因此：

- 可以先在 parent/child 共同运行过的任务交集上做离线 pilot；
- 但不能据此证明对 500 题全池的召回能力；
- 主实验需要选一批真实 mutation，对 parent 和 child 跑一次较大的统一集合，形成 `mutation × task × outcome` ground-truth matrix，再离线模拟不同预算的 sampler。

---

## 10. 最值得强调的研究创新点

可以将论文问题表述为：

> 现有 benchmark subset selection 主要选择“具有代表性的任务”来估计总体能力；我们选择“对当前 mutation 最有诊断价值的任务”，用于判断进化边是否产生了有效改进或有害回归。

核心区别：

| 方法 | 条件信息 | 优化目标 |
|---|---|---|
| DGM 固定 subset | 无 | 固定能力估计 |
| trajectory coreset | 历史行为 | 总体分数估计 |
| predictive test selection | code change + 历史结果 | 故障召回 |
| 本方案 | mutation + task + bad-case trajectory | mutation 差分检测与回退决策 |

我建议最终方法定位为：

**Mutation-Conditioned Active Regression Evaluation**

其核心不是单纯的 RAG，而是：

```text
retrieval candidate generation
+ change-impact prediction
+ diversity-aware experimental design
+ paired causal evaluation
+ calibrated rollback decision
```

其中最关键的两个设计是：

1. **同时召回 parent 的失败任务和成功任务**，分别检测修复与回归；
2. **定向测试与全局估计分开**，不能把 retrieval Top‑K 的通过率直接当作 archive score。
````

````markdown
## 1. Agentic Search 是否适合四路召回

**我同意采用多轮、自适应的 agentic search，但不同意它能完全消除超参数。**

它可以消除四路召回的固定配额和类似：

\[
\alpha s_{\text{fix}}+\beta s_{\text{regression}}+\gamma s_{\text{representative}}+\rho s_{\text{exploration}}
\]

这样的人工权重；但仍然需要少量明确参数：

- 总评测预算；
- 单轮 batch 大小；
- 最大检索轮数；
- accept/rollback 的统计阈值；
- 强制随机审计的最低预算；
- 不确定时的最大扩容预算。

如果全部交给模型，这些权重不会消失，只是变成 prompt 和模型行为中的**隐式超参数**，更难复现和审计。

### 推荐改法：四路召回变成四类工具，而不是四个固定配额

```text
Agentic Evaluation Search
│
├── search_repair_cases()
├── search_regression_cases()
├── search_representative_cases()
├── inspect_task_history(task_ids)
├── inspect_trajectories(task_ids)
├── measure_coverage(candidate_ids, selected_ids)
└── request_paired_evaluation(task_ids)
```

模型根据当前证据自行决定：

1. 调用哪一路；
2. 如何改写 query；
3. 是否需要查看具体 trajectory；
4. 下一轮应扩展哪个 failure cluster；
5. 当前证据缺的是什么。

但最终任务 ID 必须来自数据集索引，模型不能凭空生成。

### 建议的迭代过程

```text
输入：
- mutation intent
- actual diff
- parent task history
- parent bad-case diagnoses
- 总预算 B

Round 1:
1. 分析 diff，生成可能改善和可能破坏的行为契约
2. 检索高概率 repair cases
3. 检索高概率 regression cases
4. 加入少量全局代表样本和随机审计样本
5. parent/child 配对执行

Round 2:
1. 观察哪些任务发生 parent/child outcome flip
2. 更新改动影响假设
3. 围绕新发现的 regression/improvement 搜索同类任务
4. 补足未覆盖的行为区域
5. 再做配对执行

Round 3...:
- regression 出现：扩展其影响范围
- 只发现 improvement：主动搜索反例和副作用
- 全部 unchanged：转向未覆盖区域
- 证据已经足够：停止
- 预算耗尽仍不确定：quarantine/escalate
```

### 必须保留两个非 agentic 部分

#### 1. 随机审计不能让模型选择

如果“探索样本”也是模型选择的，它仍然会受模型先验影响，不是真正的 exploration。

因此：

```text
S_random = seeded_stratified_random_sample(...)
```

必须由独立、可复现的随机程序生成。模型可以看到结果，但不能决定这些任务是谁。

#### 2. 最终回退决策不应只由模型输出

模型适合：

- 分析改动；
- 生成检索 query；
- 诊断失败；
- 解释为什么继续采样；
- 提议下一批任务。

最终 `accept / rollback / escalate` 应由配对执行结果和确定性规则决定。否则检索模型既提出假设又裁决假设，容易形成 confirmation bias。

### 推荐总体结构

```text
LLM agent
  └─ 提出“接下来最值得验证什么”

Retrieval/index
  └─ 返回真实候选、历史证据、coverage 信息

Deterministic scheduler
  └─ 加入随机审计、约束预算、去除重复候选

Paired evaluator
  └─ 在相同 task/seed 上执行 parent 和 child

Decision engine
  └─ 根据真实结果决定 accept / rollback / escalate
```

这可以称为：

> **Agentic Adaptive Evaluation Search**

---

## 2. Coverage 和 Redundancy 如何计算

它们的目的不同：

- **Relevance**：任务是否很可能被本次 mutation 影响。
- **Coverage**：所选任务是否覆盖了候选池中的不同任务类型和行为模式。
- **Redundancy**：预算是否浪费在高度相似、可能给出重复证据的任务上。

### 一个具体例子

假设修改了 context compaction，相关性 Top‑10 可能全部是：

```text
Django + 长 trajectory + context overflow
```

这些任务相关性很高，但行为模式几乎相同。如果只跑它们：

- 能发现 Django 长上下文回归；
- 可能漏掉多文件编辑、跨工具状态、长测试输出等其他 context 问题。

Coverage 用于覆盖这些不同模式；Redundancy 用于避免 10 道题提供几乎同一份证据。

---

### 2.1 Task representation

先将每个任务表示成向量 \(z_t\)。建议把以下信息序列化成统一的 `TaskCard` 后做 embedding：

```text
TaskCard:
- issue/problem statement
- repository/language/task type
- parent outcome
- parent failure diagnosis
- trajectory summary
- tools/actions used
- files edited
- error categories
- context/token/step statistics
```

注意不要直接嵌入完整原始 trajectory，容易被 repo 名称、测试输出和 outcome 文本主导。应先清洗和结构化。

---

### 2.2 Coverage：Facility Location

最适合这里的定义是 facility-location coverage：

\[
C(S)
=
\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}
w_t
\max_{s\in S}
\operatorname{sim}(z_t,z_s)
\]

其中：

- \(\mathcal T\)：总任务池或本轮候选池；
- \(S\)：已选择的评测子集；
- `sim`：cosine similarity，归一化到 \([0,1]\)；
- \(w_t\)：任务权重。

直观解释：

> 对总池中的每个任务，找到 selected subset 中最像它的任务；越相似，说明这个任务所属的行为区域被覆盖得越好。

归一化后：

\[
C_{\text{norm}}(S)
=
\frac{
\sum_t w_t\max_{s\in S}\operatorname{sim}(z_t,z_s)
}{
\sum_t w_t
}
\]

其取值在 \([0,1]\) 附近：

- 接近 1：绝大部分任务都有相似代表；
- 较低：存在大片未覆盖区域。

#### 新增候选的 marginal coverage

选择下一道题时，更有用的是：

\[
\Delta C(x\mid S)=C(S\cup\{x\})-C(S)
\]

如果 \(x\) 与已选任务非常相似，它的增量接近 0；如果它代表一个新区域，增量较大。

因此 facility location 本身已经具有“收益递减”特性。

---

### 2.3 避免大类支配 coverage

如果 Django 占数据集 60%，普通 facility location 可能主要优化 Django coverage。

可以先将任务按 joint embedding 或结构化标签划分为 \(K\) 个 cluster，然后令：

\[
w_t=\frac{1}{K|G(t)|}
\]

其中 \(G(t)\) 是任务所属 cluster。

这样每个 cluster 的总权重相同，权重由数据分布自动确定，而不是人工调参。

关键安全类别建议使用硬约束，而不是权重，例如：

```text
至少覆盖：
- parent-pass regression candidates
- parent-fail repair candidates
- cold-start/no-history tasks
- critical behavior contracts
```

---

### 2.4 Redundancy

常见定义是平均 pairwise similarity：

\[
R(S)
=
\frac{2}{|S|(|S|-1)}
\sum_{i<j}
\operatorname{sim}(z_i,z_j)
\]

- \(R(S)\) 高：所选任务彼此相似；
- \(R(S)\) 低：所选任务较分散。

选择单个候选时，可以使用：

\[
r(x\mid S)=\max_{s\in S}\operatorname{sim}(z_x,z_s)
\]

它回答：

> 新任务与当前子集中最像的任务有多像？

---

### 2.5 是否需要同时优化 Coverage 和 Redundancy

**MVP 中不建议同时写成两个带权目标。**

因为 facility location 的 marginal gain 已经自然抑制冗余：

- 新候选和已有任务很像；
- 它不能提升其他任务的最近代表相似度；
- 因此 \(\Delta C\) 很低。

所以第一版建议：

```text
主目标：maximize marginal coverage gain per cost
Redundancy：只作为日志指标和近重复检查
```

即：

\[
x^*
=
\arg\max_x
\frac{\Delta C(x\mid S)}{\operatorname{cost}(x)}
\]

不再需要：

\[
\mu C(S)-\nu R(S)
\]

这样能少两个权重超参数。

但 agentic search 不是纯 coverage selection。推荐执行顺序是：

```text
1. LLM 根据 mutation 召回高相关候选池 C
2. 确定性 selector 在 C 中按 marginal coverage / cost 选 batch
3. 独立加入随机审计样本
```

LLM 解决 relevance，facility location 解决 diversity，二者职责分离。

---

## 3. 不使用 RL，直接调用模型 API

**完全同意。当前场景不需要 RL。**

原因是：

1. 进化节点和真实 regression 标签数量可能不足；
2. RL 会引入训练、reward 设计和策略漂移问题；
3. 基础模型已经能完成 mutation 分析、failure diagnosis 和多轮工具调用；
4. 研究重点应放在“动态实验设计和回退决策”，不应被 RL 训练复杂度稀释。

### 模型 API 的职责

直接调用冻结版本的模型 API 完成：

```text
1. mutation intent + diff → impact hypotheses
2. trajectory → structured failure diagnosis
3. impact hypothesis → retrieval queries
4. candidate evidence → semantic reranking
5. paired results → 下一轮需要验证的问题
6. 最终生成可审计解释
```

### 非模型部分

以下部分必须是确定性实现：

```text
- BM25/vector index
- task metadata filters
- seeded random audit
- coverage/redundancy 计算
- 预算核算
- parent/child paired execution
- 置信区间和 stopping rule
- accept/rollback/escalate 状态机
- 完整日志和中间候选保存
```

### 不需要训练模型，但需要积累 memory

可以保存每轮结果：

```text
EvolutionEvaluationRecord {
  mutation
  generated_hypotheses
  retrieval_queries
  all_retrieved_candidates
  selected_batches
  selection_reasons
  parent_child_results
  updated_diagnoses
  coverage_curve
  cost_curve
  final_decision
}
```

下一次进化时，将历史记录作为可检索 memory，而不是拿来训练 RL policy。

---

## 当前建议的整体方案

```text
               mutation intent + actual diff
                            │
                            ▼
                LLM impact hypothesis agent
                            │
             多轮调用四类检索工具，不设固定配额
                            │
                            ▼
                  relevant candidate pool
                            │
         ┌──────────────────┴───────────────────┐
         ▼                                      ▼
facility-location batch selector       seeded random audit
  maximize Δcoverage / cost             independent of LLM
         └──────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                            ▼
                 paired parent/child eval
                            │
                            ▼
                 update evidence and search
                            │
                ┌───────────┴───────────┐
                │ evidence sufficient?  │
                └───────────┬───────────┘
                       no /       \ yes
                         /         \
                 next search     deterministic
                                 decision engine
                           accept / rollback / escalate
```

需要明确的是：

- agentic search 可以取消四路固定比例和大部分人工相关性权重；
- coverage 不交给模型主观判断，而由 facility location 计算；
- redundancy 第一版不进入加权目标；
- 随机审计必须独立于模型；
- 不使用 RL，只使用模型 API；
- 模型负责搜索和诊断，执行结果负责最终裁决。

如果这个结构确认，下一步再检查当前代码和工程架构能否支持：

1. task/trajectory 数据索引；
2. agentic tool loop；
3. parent/child 配对执行；
4. 动态 batch 扩容；
5. coverage 与随机审计；
6. 回退决策接线；
7. 日志与中间数据持久化。

确认可实现后，再落盘完整设计文档。
````

function rejectCommand(command, cwd) {
	const withoutWorkspace = command.split(cwd).join("");
	const rules = [
		[/https?:\/\//i, "network URLs are disabled"],
		[/\b(curl|wget|ssh|scp|rsync)\b/i, "network commands are disabled"],
		[/\b(pip|pip3|npm|pnpm|yarn|brew|apt|apt-get|conda)\s+(install|download|add|view)\b/i, "package changes are disabled"],
		[/\bgit\s+(log|show|fetch|pull|clone|remote|branch|checkout|switch|reset|restore)\b/i, "Git history and state-changing commands are disabled"],
		[/\b(env\s+-u|unset)\b.*proxy/i, "proxy overrides are disabled"],
		[/\/tmp\//, "paths outside the task workspace are disabled"],
		[/\/(Users|private|opt|usr\/local)\//, "paths outside the task workspace are disabled"],
	];
	for (const [pattern, reason] of rules) {
		if (pattern.test(withoutWorkspace)) return reason;
	}
}

function isForbiddenEvaluationPath(path, excludedPrefixes, exactForbiddenPaths) {
	if (exactForbiddenPaths.includes(path)) return true;
	if (excludedPrefixes.some((prefix) => path === prefix.replace(/\/$/, "") || path.startsWith(prefix))) {
		return true;
	}
	const segments = path.split("/");
	const basename = segments.at(-1) ?? "";
	return (
		segments.some((segment) => segment === "test" || segment === "tests" || segment === "testing") ||
		basename === "conftest.py" ||
		basename.startsWith("test_") ||
		basename.endsWith("_test.py")
	);
}

function runCommand(command, cwd, image, dockerHost, executionId, timeoutSeconds, signal, onUpdate) {
	return new Promise((resolvePromise) => {
		const containerName = `pi-swe-${safeDockerName(executionId)}`;
		const dockerEnvironment = {
			...process.env,
			...(dockerHost ? { DOCKER_HOST: dockerHost } : {}),
		};
		const child = spawn("docker", [
			"run",
			"--rm",
			"--name",
			containerName,
			"--network",
			"none",
			"--cap-drop",
			"ALL",
			"--security-opt",
			"no-new-privileges",
			"--pids-limit",
			"512",
			"--read-only",
			"--tmpfs",
			"/tmp:rw,exec,nosuid,size=2g",
			"--tmpfs",
			"/root/.cache:rw,nosuid,size=1g",
			"--volume",
			`${cwd}:/testbed:rw`,
			"--workdir",
			"/testbed",
			"--env",
			"HOME=/tmp",
			"--env",
			"PIP_NO_INDEX=1",
			image,
			"/bin/bash",
			"-lc",
			command,
		], {
			env: dockerEnvironment,
		});
		let output = "";
		let timedOut = false;
		let aborted = false;
		const append = (chunk) => {
			output += chunk.toString();
			if (output.length > 100_000) output = output.slice(-100_000);
			onUpdate?.({ content: [{ type: "text", text: output }], details: { command } });
		};
		child.stdout.on("data", append);
		child.stderr.on("data", append);
		const timer = setTimeout(() => {
			timedOut = true;
			child.kill("SIGTERM");
		}, timeoutSeconds * 1000);
		signal?.addEventListener(
			"abort",
			() => {
				aborted = true;
				child.kill("SIGTERM");
			},
			{ once: true },
		);
		child.on("close", (code, childSignal) => {
			clearTimeout(timer);
			if (timedOut || aborted) {
				try {
					execFileSync("docker", ["rm", "--force", containerName], {
						env: dockerEnvironment,
						stdio: "ignore",
					});
				} catch {}
			}
			const suffix = timedOut ? `\nCommand timed out after ${timeoutSeconds}s.` : "";
			resolvePromise({
				content: [{ type: "text", text: `${output}${suffix}` || "(no output)" }],
				details: { command, exitCode: code, signal: childSignal, timedOut },
			});
		});
	});
}

async function assertWorkspacePath(path, cwd, options = {}) {
	const absolutePath = resolve(path);
	const pathFromWorkspace = relative(cwd, absolutePath);
	if (pathFromWorkspace === ".." || pathFromWorkspace.startsWith(`..${sep}`) || resolve(cwd, pathFromWorkspace) !== absolutePath) {
		throw new Error(`Path outside task workspace: ${path}`);
	}

	const components = pathFromWorkspace.split(sep).filter(Boolean);
	let current = cwd;
	for (const component of components) {
		current = resolve(current, component);
		try {
			const info = await lstat(current);
			if (info.isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error(`Symbolic links are disabled: ${current}`);
		} catch (error) {
			if (error instanceof Error && "code" in error && error.code === "ENOENT") {
				if (options.allowMissing) return absolutePath;
				throw new Error(`Path not found: ${absolutePath}`);
			}
			throw error;
		}
	}
	const canonical = await realpath(absolutePath);
	const canonicalRelative = relative(cwd, canonical);
	if (canonicalRelative === ".." || canonicalRelative.startsWith(`..${sep}`)) {
		throw new Error(`Path outside task workspace: ${path}`);
	}
	return canonical;
}

async function findWorkspaceFiles(pattern, searchPath, workspacePath, limit) {
	const root = await assertWorkspacePath(searchPath, workspacePath);
	const matcher = globMatcher(pattern);
	const matches = [];
	const visit = async (directory, prefix) => {
		if (matches.length >= limit) return;
		const entries = await readdir(directory, { withFileTypes: true });
		entries.sort((left, right) => left.name.localeCompare(right.name));
		for (const entry of entries) {
			if (matches.length >= limit) return;
			if (entry.name === ".git" || entry.name === "node_modules") continue;
			const entryPath = resolve(directory, entry.name);
			const relativePath = prefix ? `${prefix}/${entry.name}` : entry.name;
			if (entry.isSymbolicLink()) continue;
			if (entry.isDirectory()) {
				await visit(entryPath, relativePath);
			} else if (entry.isFile() && matcher(relativePath, entry.name)) {
				matches.push(entryPath);
			}
		}
	};
	await visit(root, "");
	return matches;
}

function globMatcher(pattern) {
	const useFullPath = pattern.includes("/");
	let expression = "^";
	for (let index = 0; index < pattern.length; index += 1) {
		const character = pattern[index];
		if (character === "*" && pattern[index + 1] === "*") {
			if (pattern[index + 2] === "/") {
				expression += "(?:.*/)?";
				index += 2;
			} else {
				expression += ".*";
				index += 1;
			}
		} else if (character === "*") {
			expression += "[^/]*";
		} else if (character === "?") {
			expression += "[^/]";
		} else {
			expression += character.replace(/[|\\{}()[\]^$+?.]/g, "\\$&");
		}
	}
	expression += "$";
	const regex = new RegExp(expression);
	return (relativePath, basename) => regex.test(useFullPath ? relativePath : basename);
}

function safeDockerName(value) {
	const normalized = value.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9_.-]+/g, "-").replace(/^[^a-z0-9]+/, "");
	const suffix = createHash("sha256").update(value).digest("hex").slice(0, 10);
	return `${normalized.slice(0, 45) || "task"}-${suffix}`;
}

# Pre-Registration: DGM 200-Task Pi and RF-CLM Evaluation

Date frozen: 2026-09-25

## Research Question

Measure quality, model-token use, evaluator cost, and wall time for fixed
original Pi and the current RF-CLM recovery workflow on the exact 200
SWE-bench Verified tasks used by DGM.

The released DGM result is a historical reference, not a causal same-model
baseline. DGM used a different coding agent, model, search budget, and
multi-week evolution process.

## Frozen Data

- DGM source commit:
  `682eb38a3eb232f4396924cacd0a083bf1444cf8`
- DGM partitions: disjoint `small=10`, `medium=50`, `big=140`
- SWE-bench Verified revision:
  `c104f840cc67f8b6eec6f759ebc8b2693d585d4a`
- Execution order: source Verified row order filtered by DGM membership
- Ordered ID hash:
  `421c950302366954005dab020cdc89ca0d6ae1f0423e2b662637f7790a31d0d7`
- Frozen manifest:
  `dgm_swebench_verified_200.v1.json`
- Manifest hash:
  `3fb913fbc73a05c1f7cae3b708c976374632820b58377aab5de08b742f96c967`

The manifest contains the complete 13-field official rows. Agent workspaces
receive only `instance_id`, `repo`, `base_commit`, and `problem_statement`.
Gold patches, test patches, and official evaluator outcomes are never mounted
into an agent workspace.

## Protocols

### P1: Original Pi one-shot

- Package: `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.85.1`
- Model: `byteplus/deepseek-v4-flash-ga`
- One isolated Pi session per task
- Maximum 512,000 reported tokens and 3,600 seconds per task
- Exact base commit, no remote, no future Git refs
- File tools confined to the task workspace
- Shell commands run in the task image with `--network none`
- Tests and other excluded paths cannot enter the submitted patch
- No official evaluator result is returned to Pi

This is the primary standard SWE-bench arm and the only local arm placed in a
direct accuracy table beside DGM's published 200-task score.

### P2: Pi + RF-CLM, one evaluator-feedback recovery

P2 starts from P1. Only unresolved P1 tasks are eligible for one bounded
causal-slice repair call. The repair receives the task statement, rejected
patch, official failure evidence, and source files already selected by the P1
patch. The final combined patch is graded once under a content-addressed run
ID.

P2 is explicitly labeled **feedback-assisted recovery**. It is an operational
upper bound and is not a standard one-submission SWE-bench score. It must not
be presented as directly equivalent to DGM's reported 50%.

No second repair, manual edit, task-specific prompt, or post-hoc task exclusion
is allowed.

## Hypotheses

### H12: Fixed original-Pi endpoint

**Prediction.** P1 resolves 40%-60% of the 200 tasks. This range is based on
the prior 5/10 DGM-small pilot and is not a power-derived claim.

**Kill criterion.** Reject any conclusion about P1 if hidden evaluator
information, future Git history, external files, or network access reaches the
agent. Infrastructure/provider failures remain failures in the
intention-to-evaluate primary score; a separately labeled per-protocol
sensitivity analysis may exclude only failures proven unrelated to the patch.

### H13: RF-CLM recovery gain

**Prediction.** P2 improves absolute solve rate by 5-20 percentage points over
P1 with no more than 20% additional reported model tokens.

**Kill criterion.** The endpoint gain claim is rejected if the paired
task-level 95% bootstrap interval for `P2 - P1` includes zero. The low-cost
claim is rejected if recovery adds more than 20% reported model tokens, or if
it does not reduce cost relative to a quality-matched full Pi retry.

The quality-matched retry comparison is required before claiming that RF-CLM
is cheaper than retrying Pi. If no retry arm is run, only recovery overhead is
reported.

## Metrics

### Primary quality

- Resolved tasks and solve rate over all 200 frozen tasks
- Wilson 95% interval for each solve rate
- Paired task difference `P2 - P1`
- Paired bootstrap 95% interval, 10,000 resamples, seed `20260925`
- Exact McNemar/binomial test over discordant task outcomes

Because P2 is a recovery protocol, it should not make a resolved P1 task fail.
Any such regression is treated as a pipeline defect and reported.

### Cost and time

- Input, output, cache-read, cache-write, and total reported tokens
- Token mean, median, interquartile range, and p95 per task
- Agent summed duration and experiment elapsed wall time
- Evaluator summed runtime and build/runtime errors
- Tool calls, retries, timeouts, budget aborts, empty patches
- Recovery attempts, successes, success rate, and incremental overhead
- Estimated API cost only when externally verified per-token prices are
  supplied; the current model catalog's zero prices are not treated as free
  usage

### Historical DGM reference

- Initial agent: 20% on the paper's 60-task development evaluation
- Best released 200-task node: `100/200 = 50%`
- Evolution duration: approximately two weeks
- Reported total evolution cost: approximately `$22,000`
- Reported baseline cost: approximately `$10,000`
- Reported 60-task Claude evaluation: approximately `$350`
- DGM input/output token counts: not reported

Missing DGM token or single-200-evaluation cost values remain `not reported`;
they are not inferred from dollar totals.

## Execution and Stopping

- Tasks run in the frozen Verified order.
- Concurrency defaults to one.
- State is written atomically after every phase and is resumable.
- Evaluator run IDs hash the protocol, manifest, model, instance, and patch.
- A global reported-token cap and elapsed-time cap are checked between tasks.
- Paid execution requires an explicit command-line confirmation value.
- The cheapest killing test is a no-model validation followed by one
  infrastructure-only task. Full 200-task model execution starts only after
  the projected token/time budget is reviewed and approved.

## Scope Limits

This run has 200 paired tasks but only one stochastic generation pass per
system. Task-level intervals do not estimate model-run variance. A
publication-level stochastic superiority claim requires at least three
independent generation seeds or repeats under the same protocol and budget.

The experiment evaluates fixed Pi plus a feedback recovery workflow. It does
not reproduce DGM's open-ended self-evolution search and cannot attribute any
difference to RF-CLM versus DGM's evolutionary mechanism.

## Post-Start Operational Amendments

At task 5 (`astropy__astropy-13453`), the gateway rejected the initial model
request with `RATE_LIMIT_TPM_EXCEEDED` before returning any usage or patch.
This attempt was quarantined under `dgm200_run/invalid_attempts/` and is
excluded from all metrics. It will be rerun from the frozen input without
receiving evaluator feedback from the invalid attempt.

Starting with that rerun, a fixed 90-second delay is inserted between tasks to
keep sequential requests below the externally imposed 1,000,000 TPM limit.
This changes only request pacing, not prompts, model settings, task order,
per-task budgets, grading, or either protocol's information access.

The task-5 rerun later reached the same TPM limit after producing 487,145
reported tokens and a valid patch. That patch passed the official evaluator,
so the attempt remains in the primary results. Starting after task 5, the
stateless SSE adapter also retries only upstream HTTP 429 responses, at most
three times with at least 65 seconds between attempts. The retried request body
is identical. Proxy hashes and the exact applicability boundary are recorded
in `dgm200_run/runtime_amendments.json`.

Task 6 then encountered two pre-generation image-build failures caused by
15-second PyPI read/TLS timeouts. Starting with the task-6 retry, Docker builds
set build-only `PIP_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT=120` and `PIP_RETRIES=20` arguments. This
changes network failure tolerance only; dependency specifications, source
commits, image platforms, and runtime environments remain unchanged. The
builder hashes and applicability boundary are recorded in the same amendment
file.

The first resumed pass encountered another PyPI index failure on task 7 and
then stopped after task 8 because the repair model returned an `old` string
that occurred three times. Task 8's P1 result is valid. Its sole P2 call is
retained as a failed repair attempt; it is not retried. The pre-amendment
repair runner raised before persisting that response's usage, so exact token
telemetry for this one call is unavailable. A conservative 512,000-token
charge is applied to the global cap, while reported-token distributions mark
the sample missing rather than imputing fabricated input/output counts.

Starting after this incident, repair telemetry is persisted before edit
application, and exact-edit validation failures are terminal P2 failures
rather than infrastructure errors. This changes failure accounting and
resumability only; it does not change prompts, model calls, eligibility,
official grading, or the one-repair limit. Official evaluator failures remain
infrastructure errors. Exact hashes and the task-level accounting record are
in `dgm200_run/runtime_amendments.json`.

Task 12 then reproduced the same transient PyPI index failure while resolving
unchanged Astropy build dependencies. Its no-model attempt was discarded.
Starting with the task-12 retry, those exact PyPI wheels are read from a local,
SHA-256-manifested wheelhouse with `PIP_NO_INDEX=1`. The same wheelhouse remains
available to the official evaluator because it repeats the editable install
inside the task container. It contains only public third-party build
dependencies, no task source, patches, tests, or evaluator outcomes. The
builder also retries image-only failures twice. Completed-task skips no longer
incur the 90-second model pacing delay, and the wall-time cap is measured from
the original run start across resumptions. None of these changes affects model
inputs, dependency versions, task source, or evaluator commands. The wheel
hashes and image verification are recorded in
`dgm200_run/runtime_amendments.json`.

# Pi evals

Pi evals are behavioral, model-backed checks for Pi workflows. They adapt a real `AgentSession` to `vitest-evals`, run
it in isolated temporary project and agent directories, and attach native Pi session artifacts.
Use them to measure end-to-end behavior and compare prompts, tools, skills, models, or other harness configurations.

## Running evals

Run from the repository root with a default provider and model:

```bash
npm run eval -- --provider openai --model gpt-5.6-sol
```

The equivalent environment variables are:

```bash
PI_PROVIDER=openai PI_MODEL=gpt-5.6-sol npm run eval
```

CLI values take precedence and become defaults for harnesses that do not select a model explicitly. Provider and model must be supplied together. The runner also allows no default when every executed harness configures its own model.
Authentication comes from Pi's normal `ModelRuntime`, including Pi subscription credentials and provider API-key
environment variables.

Additional arguments are forwarded to Vitest:

```bash
npm run eval -- src/extensions.eval.ts
npm run eval -- -t "creates and uses the extension"
npm run eval -- src/docs.eval.ts -t "session-format\.md"
```

Run all comparative customization evals five times in one invocation:

```bash
npm run eval -- \
  src/extensions.eval.ts src/models.eval.ts src/providers.eval.ts \
  --provider openai --model gpt-5.6-sol \
  --repetitions 5
```

`--repetitions` applies to suites declared with `evalHarnessTable(...)`. An explicit `repetitions` value in a suite
overrides the command-line default. `PI_EVAL_REPETITIONS=5` is equivalent to the command-line option. Use one repetition
while developing an eval and five when reporting lift.

## Reports and artifacts

Each invocation prints a compound `Eval Comparisons` report after the Vitest results. When several comparative files run
in the same invocation, this report contains one section for every eval set. For example, with illustrative values:

```text
Eval Comparisons
  Add model to existing provider
     Baseline  system-prompt-without-docs
    Candidate  default-system-prompt (5/5 pairs)
    Pass rate  +60.0 pp (candidate 80.0%, baseline 20.0%)
       Tokens  +1200.0 (candidate 24000.0, baseline 22800.0)
      Latency  -850.0ms (candidate 14000.0ms, baseline 14850.0ms)
    Est. cost  +$0.0100 (candidate $0.1200, baseline $0.1100)

  Add OpenAI-compatible provider
    ...

  Add custom streaming provider
    ...
```

The runner prints the ignored `.eval/` artifact directory at startup. It contains:

- `report.txt`: the terminal comparison report without color codes.
- `report.json`: the same aggregate comparison data as structured JSON.
- `runs.jsonl`: one record for every completed harness run.
- `sessions/`: native Pi session JSONL attachments.
- `sources/`: source attachments recorded by individual evals.

The report covers comparative suites using `evalHarnessTable(...)`. Ordinary evals still appear in the Vitest summary and
in `runs.jsonl`, but not in the baseline-versus-candidate comparison report. Artifacts may contain prompts, responses,
source code, and tool output.

## Writing evals

Follow [`vitest-evals`](https://github.com/getsentry/vitest-evals) for general suite, judge, assertion, and normalized
trace guidance. Pi-specific evals use `createPiCodingAgentHarness(...)` from `src/pi-harness.ts`, with one harness bound
to each `describeEval(...)` suite:

```ts
import { expect } from "vitest";
import { describeEval } from "vitest-evals";
import { createPiCodingAgentHarness } from "./pi-harness.ts";

const harness = createPiCodingAgentHarness({ noTools: "all" });

describeEval("Pi smoke", { harness }, (it) => {
	it("answers a factual question", async ({ run }) => {
		const result = await run("What is the capital of France? Reply with only the city name.");
		expect(result.output).toBe("Paris");
	});
});
```

### Configuring the Pi harness

`createPiCodingAgentHarness(...)` accepts:

- `name`: stable harness identity used by reports and comparisons.
- `model`: optional `{ provider, id }` selection. It overrides the runner's default model.
- `noTools`: Pi's tool-disable configuration.
- `tools`: optional allowlist of tool names available to the evaluated agent.
- `customTools`: custom tool definitions to register for the evaluated agent.
- `transformSystemPrompt`: transforms the complete default prompt before the eval starts.
- `output`: transforms the final response and `AgentSession` into a JSON-safe domain result.

An explicitly selected model makes model-comparison harnesses independent of the runner default:

```ts
const harness = createPiCodingAgentHarness({
	name: "claude-opus-4-6",
	model: { provider: "anthropic", id: "claude-opus-4-6" },
});
```

A run accepts either one prompt or a sequence of prompt and reload steps. Reload steps are useful when the preceding
prompt creates or changes Pi resources:

```ts
const result = await run([
	{ type: "prompt", content: "Create a Pi extension." },
	{ type: "reload" },
	{ type: "prompt", content: "Use the extension." },
]);
```

### Transforming harness output

Use `output` to expose scenario-specific, JSON-safe behavior without adding that behavior to the generic Pi adapter:

```ts
const harness = createPiCodingAgentHarness({
	output: ({ response, session }) => ({
		response,
		activeTools: session.getActiveToolNames(),
		extensionErrors: session.resourceLoader.getExtensions().errors,
	}),
});
```

Assert application behavior on `result.output`. Assert model and tool traces on `result.session`, using
`vitest-evals` helpers such as `toolCalls(...)`.

### Writing comparative eval sets

Use `evalHarnessTable(...)` with Vitest's native `describe.for(...)` to run the same inputs against multiple harnesses.
Harnesses may differ by prompt, tools, skills, model, or any other Pi configuration:

```ts
import { describe } from "vitest";
import { createJudge, describeEval } from "vitest-evals";
import { evalHarnessTable } from "./vitest-evals/harness-table.ts";

const TargetTaskJudge = createJudge<string, string>("TargetTaskJudge", ({ output }) => ({
	score: output === "expected result" ? 1 : 0,
}));

const harnessTable = evalHarnessTable(
	"target skill effectiveness",
	{
		baseline: withoutTargetSkillHarness,
		candidate: withTargetSkillHarness,
		repetitions: 6,
	},
);

describe.for(harnessTable)("$name repetition $repetition", ({ harness }) => {
	describeEval("target skill effectiveness", { harness, judges: [TargetTaskJudge], judgeThreshold: null }, (it) => {
		it("completes the target task", async ({ run }) => {
			await run("Complete the target task.");
		});
	});
});
```

Comparative suites should record correctness with deterministic or model-backed judges and set `judgeThreshold: null`.
This keeps a low score as an observation instead of making the Vitest invocation fail. Use hard assertions only for
suite invariants and infrastructure contracts. `expect.soft(...)` still fails the test and is not a scoring mechanism.

The Pi harness snapshots native session JSONL before deleting its temporary workspace. An eval-only `afterEach` hook
registers that snapshot against the explicit Vitest test task before reporters run.

Harness names must be stable and unique within an eval set. The grouping key combines repetition with a non-empty string
`input.id` when available, otherwise with a SHA-256 hash of strict canonical JSON input. Use `candidate` for one treatment
or `candidates` for multiple treatments. Each candidate is compared only with the declared baseline. For each matched
input and repetition, the reporter computes pass-rate lift from each run's recorded average judge score, treating a score
of at least `1` as passing. Lift is the candidate pass rate minus the baseline pass rate, in percentage points. Missing
judge scores are reported as incomplete observations. Tokens, latency, and estimated cost remain separate
candidate-minus-baseline paired deltas; missing telemetry remains unavailable. If execution-order randomization becomes
necessary, use Vitest's built-in sequence shuffling.

See the [`skill-eval-harness`](https://github.com/adewale/skill-eval-harness/) guidance for comparative-eval methodology,
repetition strategy, trustworthy judges, and telemetry interpretation.

--- pi-harness ---
import { existsSync } from "node:fs";
import { mkdir, mkdtemp, readFile, rm } from "node:fs/promises";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { performance } from "node:perf_hooks";
import { contentText } from "@earendil-works/pi-ai";
import {
	type AgentSession,
	type CreateAgentSessionOptions,
	createAgentSessionFromServices,
	createAgentSessionServices,
	type InlineExtension,
	ModelRuntime,
	SessionManager,
	SettingsManager,
} from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent";
import {
	createHarness,
	type Harness,
	type HarnessContext,
	type JsonValue,
	normalizeRecord,
	type SimpleHarnessResult,
	type TranscriptEvent,
	toJsonValue,
} from "vitest-evals/harness";
import { PI_SESSION_SNAPSHOT_ARTIFACT } from "./vitest-evals/artifacts.ts";

export type PiCodingAgentInput = string | Array<{ type: "prompt"; content: string } | { type: "reload" }>;

type PiCodingAgentModelSelection = {
	provider: string;
	id: string;
};

type PiCodingAgentHarnessOptions = {
	name?: string;
	model?: PiCodingAgentModelSelection;
	noTools?: CreateAgentSessionOptions["noTools"];
	tools?: CreateAgentSessionOptions["tools"];
	customTools?: CreateAgentSessionOptions["customTools"];
	transformSystemPrompt?: (defaultPrompt: string) => string;
};

type PiCodingAgentHarnessWithOutput<TOutput extends JsonValue> = PiCodingAgentHarnessOptions & {
	output: (args: {
		response: string;
		session: AgentSession;
		systemPrompt: string;
		agentDir: string;
	}) => TOutput | Promise<TOutput>;
};

// Comparative evals intentionally remove the documentation block using stable prompt markers instead of changing Pi's
// production prompt builder. The isolated eval prompt has no project context or skills between these markers. If
// that setup changes, this transform must be updated so baseline and candidate still differ only by documentation.
export function excludePiDocumentation(defaultPrompt: string): string {
	const documentationStart = defaultPrompt.indexOf("\nPi documentation (read only");
	if (documentationStart === -1) throw new Error("Default Pi system prompt has no Pi documentation section.");
	const cwdStart = defaultPrompt.lastIndexOf("\nCurrent working directory: ");
	if (cwdStart === -1) throw new Error("Default Pi system prompt has no working-directory section.");
	return defaultPrompt.slice(0, documentationStart) + defaultPrompt.slice(cwdStart);
}

export function resolveModelSelection(
	explicitModel: PiCodingAgentModelSelection | undefined,
	environment: { PI_PROVIDER?: string; PI_MODEL?: string } = process.env,
): PiCodingAgentModelSelection {
	const provider = (explicitModel?.provider ?? environment.PI_PROVIDER)?.trim();
	const id = (explicitModel?.id ?? environment.PI_MODEL)?.trim();
	if (!provider || !id) {
		throw new Error("Select a harness model explicitly or set both PI_PROVIDER and PI_MODEL as defaults.");
	}
	return { provider, id };
}

function toTranscriptEvents(messages: AgentSession["messages"]): TranscriptEvent[] {
	const events: TranscriptEvent[] = [];
	for (const message of messages) {
		if (message.role === "user") {
			events.push({ type: "message", role: "user", content: contentText(message.content) });
		} else if (message.role === "assistant") {
			const text = contentText(message.content);
			if (text) events.push({ type: "message", role: "assistant", content: text });
			for (const part of message.content) {
				if (part.type === "toolCall") {
					events.push({
						type: "tool_call",
						id: part.id,
						name: part.name,
						arguments: normalizeRecord(part.arguments),
					});
				}
			}
		} else if (message.role === "toolResult") {
			const text = contentText(message.content);
			events.push({
				type: "tool_result",
				toolCallId: message.toolCallId,
				name: message.toolName,
				content: message.content.every((part) => part.type === "text") ? text : toJsonValue(message.content),
				...(message.isError ? { error: { message: text || "Tool failed" } } : {}),
			});
		}
	}
	return events;
}

async function promptAgent(session: AgentSession, input: string, signal: AbortSignal | undefined): Promise<string> {
	signal?.throwIfAborted();
	const previousMessageCount = session.messages.length;
	await session.prompt(input);
	const assistant = session.messages
		.slice(previousMessageCount)
		.reverse()
		.find((message) => message.role === "assistant");
	if (!assistant) throw new Error("Agent run completed without an assistant message.");
	if (assistant.stopReason !== "stop" && assistant.stopReason !== "toolUse") {
		throw new Error(
			assistant.errorMessage ?? `Agent run ended with unexpected stop reason: ${assistant.stopReason}.`,
		);
	}
	const output = session.getLastAssistantText();
	if (!output && assistant.stopReason === "stop") throw new Error("Agent run produced no assistant text.");
	return output ?? "";
}

async function runPiCodingAgent<TOutput extends JsonValue>(
	input: PiCodingAgentInput,
	signal: AbortSignal | undefined,
	setArtifact: HarnessContext["setArtifact"],
	options: PiCodingAgentHarnessOptions | PiCodingAgentHarnessWithOutput<TOutput>,
): Promise<SimpleHarnessResult<string | TOutput>> {
	const startedAt = performance.now();
	signal?.throwIfAborted();
	const selection = resolveModelSelection(options.model);
	const modelRuntime = await ModelRuntime.create();
	const model = modelRuntime.getModel(selection.provider, selection.id);
	if (!model) throw new Error(`Eval model not found: ${selection.provider}/${selection.id}`);

	const root = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "pi-eval-"));
	const cwd = join(root, "workspace");
	const isolatedHome = join(root, "home");
	const agentDir = join(isolatedHome, ".pi", "agent");
	const transformSystemPrompt = options.transformSystemPrompt;
	let evaluatedSystemPrompt: string | undefined;
	const extensionFactories: InlineExtension[] = [];
	if (transformSystemPrompt) {
		extensionFactories.push({
			name: "eval-system-prompt-transform",
			hidden: true,
			factory: (pi) => {
				pi.on("before_agent_start", (event) => {
					evaluatedSystemPrompt = transformSystemPrompt(event.systemPrompt);
					return { systemPrompt: evaluatedSystemPrompt };
				});
			},
		});
	}
	let sessionManager: SessionManager | undefined;
	let session: AgentSession | undefined;
	let outcome: { success: true; result: SimpleHarnessResult<string | TOutput> } | { success: false; error: unknown };
	try {
		await Promise.all([mkdir(cwd), mkdir(agentDir, { recursive: true })]);
		const services = await createAgentSessionServices({
			cwd,
			agentDir,
			modelRuntime,
			settingsManager: SettingsManager.inMemory({
				shellCommandPrefix: `export HOME=${JSON.stringify(isolatedHome)}; unset PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR PI_EVAL_ARTIFACT_DIR PI_MODEL PI_PROVIDER PI_REASONING_LEVEL PI_SESSION_FILE PI_SESSION_ID;`,
			}),
			...(extensionFactories.length > 0 ? { resourceLoaderOptions: { extensionFactories } } : {}),
		});
		signal?.throwIfAborted();
		sessionManager = SessionManager.create(cwd, join(root, "sessions"));
		setArtifact("runId", sessionManager.getSessionId());
		session = (
			await createAgentSessionFromServices({
				services,
				sessionManager,
				model,
				thinkingLevel: "off",
				tools: options.tools,
				noTools: options.noTools,
				customTools: options.customTools,
			})
		).session;

		const evalSession = session;
		let abortPromise: Promise<void> | undefined;
		const abort = () => {
			abortPromise ??= evalSession.abort();
		};
		signal?.addEventListener("abort", abort, { once: true });
		try {
			signal?.throwIfAborted();
			const unexpectedExtensionPaths = evalSession.extensionRunner
				.getExtensionPaths()
				.filter((path) => path !== "<inline:eval-system-prompt-transform>");
			if (unexpectedExtensionPaths.length !== 0) {
				throw new Error("Expected an isolated eval session to start without extensions.");
			}
			const steps = typeof input === "string" ? [{ type: "prompt" as const, content: input }] : input;
			let response: string | undefined;
			for (const step of steps) {
				if (step.type === "prompt") {
					response = await promptAgent(evalSession, step.content, signal);
					if (transformSystemPrompt && !evaluatedSystemPrompt?.trim()) {
						throw new Error("System-prompt transform did not produce a non-empty prompt.");
					}
				} else {
					await evalSession.reload();
				}
			}
			if (response === undefined) throw new Error("Pi eval input must include at least one prompt step.");
			const output =
				"output" in options
					? await options.output({
							response,
							session: evalSession,
							systemPrompt: evaluatedSystemPrompt ?? evalSession.systemPrompt,
							agentDir,
						})
					: response;
			const stats = evalSession.getSessionStats();
			const hasPricing = [model.cost, ...(model.cost.tiers ?? [])].some(
				({ input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite }) => input > 0 || output > 0 || cacheRead > 0 || cacheWrite > 0,
			);
			outcome = {
				success: true,
				result: {
					output,
					events: toTranscriptEvents(evalSession.messages),
					usage: {
						provider: model.provider,
						model: model.id,
						inputTokens: stats.tokens.input,
						outputTokens: stats.tokens.output,
						totalTokens: stats.tokens.total,
						toolCalls: stats.toolCalls,
						metadata: {
							cacheReadTokens: stats.tokens.cacheRead,
							cacheWriteTokens: stats.tokens.cacheWrite,
							...(hasPricing ? { estimatedCostUsd: stats.cost } : {}),
						},
					},
				},
			};
		} finally {
			signal?.removeEventListener("abort", abort);
			if (abortPromise) await abortPromise;
		}
	} catch (error) {
		outcome = { success: false, error };
	}

	const cleanupErrors: unknown[] = [];
	if (sessionManager) {
		try {
			const sessionPath = sessionManager.getSessionFile();
			if (sessionPath && existsSync(sessionPath)) {
				setArtifact(PI_SESSION_SNAPSHOT_ARTIFACT, await readFile(sessionPath, "utf8"));
			}
		} catch (error) {
			cleanupErrors.push(error);
		}
	}
	try {
		session?.dispose();
	} catch (error) {
		cleanupErrors.push(error);
	}
	try {
		await rm(root, { recursive: true, force: true });
	} catch (error) {
		cleanupErrors.push(error);
	}

	if (!outcome.success) {
		if (cleanupErrors.length === 0) throw outcome.error;
		throw new AggregateError([outcome.error, ...cleanupErrors], "Agent run failed and cleanup also failed.");
	}
	if (cleanupErrors.length === 1) throw cleanupErrors[0];
	if (cleanupErrors.length > 1) throw new AggregateError(cleanupErrors, "Agent cleanup failed.");
	return {
		...outcome.result,
		timings: { totalMs: performance.now() - startedAt },
	};
}

export function createPiCodingAgentHarness<TOutput extends JsonValue>(
	options: PiCodingAgentHarnessWithOutput<TOutput>,
): Harness<PiCodingAgentInput, TOutput>;
export function createPiCodingAgentHarness(options?: PiCodingAgentHarnessOptions): Harness<PiCodingAgentInput, string>;
export function createPiCodingAgentHarness<TOutput extends JsonValue>(
	options: PiCodingAgentHarnessOptions | PiCodingAgentHarnessWithOutput<TOutput> = {},
) {
	return createHarness<PiCodingAgentInput, string | TOutput>({
		name: options.name ?? "pi-coding-agent",
		run: ({ input, signal, setArtifact }) => runPiCodingAgent(input, signal, setArtifact, options),
	});
}

--- harness-table ---
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import {
	attachHarnessRunToError,
	getHarnessRunFromError,
	type Harness,
	type HarnessRun,
	type JsonValue,
} from "vitest-evals/harness";

export const EVAL_HARNESS_ITERATION_ARTIFACT = "vitestEvalsHarnessIteration";

export type EvalHarnessIterationArtifact = {
	schemaVersion: 1;
	evalSet: string;
	groupKey: string;
	harness: string;
	baseline: string;
	candidates: string[];
	repetition: number;
};

export type EvalHarnessTa…2306 tokens truncated…ionPair = {
	baseline: HarnessObservation;
	candidate: HarnessObservation;
};

function getOrCreate<K, V extends object>(map: Map<K, V>, key: K, create: () => V): V {
	const existing = map.get(key);
	if (existing !== undefined) return existing;
	const value = create();
	map.set(key, value);
	return value;
}

function mean(values: readonly number[]): number | null {
	return values.length === 0 ? null : values.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0) / values.length;
}

function preciseDifference(left: number, right: number): number {
	return Number((left - right).toPrecision(15));
}

function groupObservations(observations: readonly HarnessObservation[]): Map<string, EvalSetData> {
	const evalSets = new Map<string, EvalSetData>();
	for (const observation of observations) {
		const evalSet = getOrCreate(evalSets, observation.evalSet, () => ({
			baseline: { name: observation.baseline, index: 0 },
			candidatesByName: new Map(),
			groupsByKey: new Map(),
		}));

		for (const [index, name] of observation.candidates.entries()) {
			const existing = evalSet.candidatesByName.get(name);
			if (!existing || index < existing.index) evalSet.candidatesByName.set(name, { name, index });
		}

		const group = getOrCreate(
			evalSet.groupsByKey,
			JSON.stringify([observation.file, observation.testName, observation.groupKey]),
			() => ({
				evalSet: observation.evalSet,
				groupKey: observation.groupKey,
				testName: observation.testName,
				file: observation.file,
				repetition: observation.repetition,
				observationsByHarness: new Map(),
			}),
		);
		getOrCreate(group.observationsByHarness, observation.harness, (): HarnessObservation[] => []).push(observation);
	}
	return evalSets;
}

function orderedHarnesses(evalSet: EvalSetData): HarnessDescriptor[] {
	return [
		evalSet.baseline,
		...[...evalSet.candidatesByName.values()].sort(
			(left, right) => left.index - right.index || left.name.localeCompare(right.name),
		),
	];
}

function orderedCandidates(evalSet: EvalSetData): HarnessDescriptor[] {
	return [...evalSet.candidatesByName.values()].sort(
		(left, right) => left.index - right.index || left.name.localeCompare(right.name),
	);
}

function orderedGroups(evalSet: EvalSetData): ObservationGroup[] {
	return [...evalSet.groupsByKey.values()].sort(
		(left, right) => left.groupKey.localeCompare(right.groupKey) || left.repetition - right.repetition,
	);
}

function collectDiagnostics(
	harnesses: readonly HarnessDescriptor[],
	groups: readonly ObservationGroup[],
): HarnessComparisonDiagnostic[] {
	const diagnostics: HarnessComparisonDiagnostic[] = [];
	for (const group of groups) {
		for (const { name: harness } of harnesses) {
			const observations = group.observationsByHarness.get(harness) ?? [];
			let reason: HarnessComparisonDiagnostic["reason"] | undefined;
			if (observations.length === 0) reason = "missing-observation";
			else if (observations.length > 1) reason = "duplicate-observation";
			else if (observations[0].outcome === "errored") reason = "harness-error";
			else if (observations[0].outcome === "unscored") {
				reason = "missing-score";
			} else if (observations[0].outcome !== "scored") {
				reason = "unscorable-outcome";
			}
			if (!reason) continue;
			diagnostics.push({
				evalSet: group.evalSet,
				groupKey: group.groupKey,
				testName: group.testName,
				file: group.file,
				repetition: group.repetition,
				harness,
				reason,
			});
		}
	}
	return diagnostics;
}

function pairObservations(
	groups: readonly ObservationGroup[],
	baselineHarness: string,
	candidateHarness: string,
): ObservationPair[] {
	const pairs: ObservationPair[] = [];
	for (const group of groups) {
		const baseline = group.observationsByHarness.get(baselineHarness) ?? [];
		const candidate = group.observationsByHarness.get(candidateHarness) ?? [];
		if (baseline.length === 1 && candidate.length === 1) {
			pairs.push({ baseline: baseline[0], candidate: candidate[0] });
		}
	}
	return pairs;
}

function summarizeMetric(
	pairs: readonly ObservationPair[],
	select: (observation: HarnessObservation) => number | undefined,
	totalPairs: number,
): PairedMetricSummary {
	const baselineValues: number[] = [];
	const candidateValues: number[] = [];
	for (const { baseline, candidate } of pairs) {
		if (baseline.outcome !== "scored" || candidate.outcome !== "scored") continue;
		const baselineValue = select(baseline);
		const candidateValue = select(candidate);
		if (
			baselineValue === undefined ||
			candidateValue === undefined ||
			!Number.isFinite(baselineValue) ||
			!Number.isFinite(candidateValue)
		) {
			continue;
		}
		baselineValues.push(baselineValue);
		candidateValues.push(candidateValue);
	}

	const baselineMean = mean(baselineValues);
	const candidateMean = mean(candidateValues);
	return {
		totalPairs,
		eligiblePairs: baselineValues.length,
		baselineMean,
		candidateMean,
		meanDelta:
			baselineMean === null || candidateMean === null ? null : preciseDifference(candidateMean, baselineMean),
	};
}

function summarizeCorrectness(pairs: readonly ObservationPair[], totalPairs: number): CorrectnessLiftSummary {
	let eligiblePairs = 0;
	let baselinePasses = 0;
	let candidatePasses = 0;
	let baselineWins = 0;
	let candidateWins = 0;
	let ties = 0;

	for (const { baseline, candidate } of pairs) {
		if (baseline.outcome !== "scored" || candidate.outcome !== "scored") continue;
		eligiblePairs += 1;
		const baselinePassed = baseline.score >= 1;
		const candidatePassed = candidate.score >= 1;
		if (baselinePassed) baselinePasses += 1;
		if (candidatePassed) candidatePasses += 1;
		if (baselinePassed === candidatePassed) ties += 1;
		else if (baselinePassed) baselineWins += 1;
		else candidateWins += 1;
	}

	const baselinePassRate = eligiblePairs === 0 ? null : baselinePasses / eligiblePairs;
	const candidatePassRate = eligiblePairs === 0 ? null : candidatePasses / eligiblePairs;
	return {
		totalPairs,
		eligiblePairs,
		baselinePassRate,
		candidatePassRate,
		lift:
			baselinePassRate === null || candidatePassRate === null
				? null
				: preciseDifference(candidatePassRate, baselinePassRate),
		baselineWins,
		candidateWins,
		ties,
	};
}

function compareHarnesses(
	baseline: HarnessDescriptor,
	candidate: HarnessDescriptor,
	groups: readonly ObservationGroup[],
): HarnessPairComparison {
	const pairs = pairObservations(groups, baseline.name, candidate.name);
	return {
		baseline: baseline.name,
		candidate: candidate.name,
		correctness: summarizeCorrectness(pairs, groups.length),
		totalTokens: summarizeMetric(pairs, ({ totalTokens }) => totalTokens, groups.length),
		totalMs: summarizeMetric(pairs, ({ totalMs }) => totalMs, groups.length),
		estimatedCostUsd: summarizeMetric(pairs, ({ estimatedCostUsd }) => estimatedCostUsd, groups.length),
	};
}

export function summarizeHarnessComparisons(observations: readonly HarnessObservation[]): HarnessComparisonReport {
	const evalSets: HarnessEvalSetReport[] = [];
	const diagnostics: HarnessComparisonDiagnostic[] = [];
	for (const [evalSet, data] of [...groupObservations(observations)].sort(([left], [right]) =>
		left.localeCompare(right),
	)) {
		const harnesses = orderedHarnesses(data);
		const candidates = orderedCandidates(data);
		const groups = orderedGroups(data);
		evalSets.push({
			evalSet,
			comparisons: candidates.map((candidate) => compareHarnesses(data.baseline, candidate, groups)),
		});
		diagnostics.push(...collectDiagnostics(harnesses, groups));
	}

	return {
		schemaVersion: 1,
		evalSets,
		diagnostics: diagnostics.sort(
			(left, right) =>
				left.evalSet.localeCompare(right.evalSet) ||
				left.file.localeCompare(right.file) ||
				left.groupKey.localeCompare(right.groupKey) ||
				left.repetition - right.repetition ||
				left.harness.localeCompare(right.harness),
		),
	};
}

function formatPercentage(value: number | null): string {
	return value === null ? "unavailable" : `${(value * 100).toFixed(1)}%`;
}

function formatSigned(value: number, fractionDigits: number): string {
	return `${value >= 0 ? "+" : ""}${value.toFixed(fractionDigits)}`;
}

function formatCoverage(eligiblePairs: number, totalPairs: number): string {
	return styleText("gray", `(${eligiblePairs}/${totalPairs} pairs)`);
}

function formatReportLine(label: string, value: string): string {
	return `    ${styleText("gray", label.padStart(9))}  ${value}`;
}

function colorDelta(value: number, formatted: string, positiveIsBetter: boolean): string {
	if (value === 0) return styleText("gray", formatted);
	const improved = positiveIsBetter ? value > 0 : value < 0;
	return styleText(improved ? "green" : "red", formatted);
}

function formatMetric(
	label: string,
	metric: PairedMetricSummary,
	formatValue: (value: number) => string,
	formatDelta: (value: number) => string,
	comparisonPairs: number,
): string {
	const coverage =
		metric.eligiblePairs === 0 || metric.eligiblePairs === comparisonPairs
			? ""
			: ` ${formatCoverage(metric.eligiblePairs, metric.totalPairs)}`;
	if (metric.baselineMean === null || metric.candidateMean === null || metric.meanDelta === null) {
		return formatReportLine(label, `${styleText("yellow", "unavailable")}${coverage}`);
	}
	const delta = colorDelta(metric.meanDelta, formatDelta(metric.meanDelta), false);
	const values = styleText(
		"gray",
		`(candidate ${formatValue(metric.candidateMean)}, baseline ${formatValue(metric.baselineMean)})`,
	);
	return formatReportLine(label, `${delta} ${values}${coverage}`);
}

export function formatHarnessComparisonReport(report: HarnessComparisonReport): string {
	if (report.evalSets.every(({ comparisons }) => comparisons.length === 0)) return "";
	const lines = [styleText("bold", "Eval Comparisons")];
	for (const evalSet of report.evalSets) {
		lines.push(`  ${evalSet.evalSet}`);
		for (const [index, comparison] of evalSet.comparisons.entries()) {
			if (index > 0) lines.push("");
			const { correctness } = comparison;
			lines.push(formatReportLine("Baseline", comparison.baseline));
			lines.push(
				formatReportLine(
					"Candidate",
					`${comparison.candidate} ${formatCoverage(correctness.eligiblePairs, correctness.totalPairs)}`,
				),
			);
			if (correctness.lift === null) {
				lines.push(formatReportLine("Pass rate", styleText("yellow", "unavailable")));
			} else {
				const lift = correctness.lift * 100;
				const delta = colorDelta(lift, `${formatSigned(lift, 1)} pp`, true);
				const values = styleText(
					"gray",
					`(candidate ${formatPercentage(correctness.candidatePassRate)}, baseline ${formatPercentage(correctness.baselinePassRate)})`,
				);
				lines.push(formatReportLine("Pass rate", `${delta} ${values}`));
			}
			lines.push(
				formatMetric(
					"Tokens",
					comparison.totalTokens,
					(value) => value.toFixed(1),
					(value) => formatSigned(value, 1),
					correctness.eligiblePairs,
				),
			);
			lines.push(
				formatMetric(
					"Latency",
					comparison.totalMs,
					(value) => `${value.toFixed(1)}ms`,
					(value) => `${formatSigned(value, 1)}ms`,
					correctness.eligiblePairs,
				),
			);
			lines.push(
				formatMetric(
					"Est. cost",
					comparison.estimatedCostUsd,
					(value) => `$${value.toFixed(4)}`,
					(value) => `${value >= 0 ? "+" : "-"}$${Math.abs(value).toFixed(4)}`,
					correctness.eligiblePairs,
				),
			);
		}
	}
	if (report.diagnostics.length > 0) {
		lines.push(`  ${styleText("yellow", "Incomplete observations")}`);
		for (const diagnostic of report.diagnostics) {
			lines.push(
				`    ${diagnostic.reason}: ${diagnostic.file}/${diagnostic.testName} repetition ${diagnostic.repetition}, harness ${diagnostic.harness}`,
			);
		}
	}
	return lines.join("\n");
}
